final.memo:
We have reviewed the business of Activision Blizzard and determined it is not a candidate for our portfolio. While the company owns recognizable franchises like Call of Duty and Candy Crush, the business requires constant creative investment to remain relevant [D01]. Unlike a wonderful business with a stable, self-maintaining royalty stream, this company’s economics depend on a continuous and unpredictable pipeline [D01].

At present, the company is embroiled in serious workplace and employment allegations [D01, D05]. We view these issues as a fundamental threat to the stability of the creative talent that is essential for the company's long-term success [D01]. When we invest, we seek honest and able managers who act as owners, but the current instability presents a risk we prefer to avoid [D01].

Furthermore, our analysis shows a year-on-year decline in net bookings [D01, D05]. This inconsistency, combined with the difficulty of normalizing owner earnings in the face of ongoing reputational and operational challenges, prevents us from identifying the margin of safety we require [D01, D02]. 

We prefer to hold cash when the risks are high and the path to future value is clouded [D08]. We remain focused on businesses we can understand and trust, and this situation falls firmly into our "too hard" pile [D01].
